recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future change to make Patient.managingOrganization repeatable would need a new Patient Administration work-group decision rather than reconciliation of FHIR-7610.
issue_request: FHIR-7610 was Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. The request asked whether Patient.managingOrganization should become 0..* for continuum-of-care scenarios or be left to Provenance; the accepted disposition kept the cardinality 0..1 and required clearer comments describing the organization as the record owner/custodian responsible for maintaining the patient record.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by git commit 58cf0bc95a3fd91d0abd717978b7898f53cfc5a3, "Tracker# 7558, 7609, 7610 Ballot recon," which added the Patient spreadsheet comment explaining that there is only one managing organization for a specific patient record and that other organizations should have their own Patient records linked together if needed. The later source refactor preserved that content in source/patient/structuredefinition-Patient.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists patient=Patient, so source/patient/structuredefinition-Patient.xml is current build-scope source. The current element has custodian wording, min 0, max 1, and the one-managing-organization comment. Later FHIR-16155 aligned the Patient organization search parameter with the same custodian wording, reinforcing rather than changing the FHIR-7610 interpretation. Direct community searches found no FHIR-7610-specific conflicting minutes or Zulip discussion; a 2020 LHS minutes item discussed a different Patient Role DAM concern and did not create a core Patient change.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the authoritative current Patient source already implements the accepted FHIR-7610 outcome.
